solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inactivity extremely self-evident in existing state of affairs

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the two extremes of the word self-evident

parts.note: things left 'as is' are in their existing state

explanation.surface: A political commentator complains that stagnation is obvious in the way things currently stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters S and T of 'self-evident'; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a period of stagnation where nothing moves or changes, a synonym for inactivity.

clue.text: Trunk examinations — not right on time

indicators.note: on means the time letter is attached to the end of what precedes it
not tells us the letter for right is dropped from the examinations word

parts.note: searches are thorough examinations of people or places

explanation.surface: Luggage inspections at the border are running late.
explanation.walkthrough: SEARCHES loses its R ('not right') to give SEACHES, and 'on' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's sturdy box for belongings is a kind of trunk, a large storage case.

clue.text: King, along with pawn on rook's square, held up major feature of key play?

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of King George
along with is another way of saying and
P is the chess notation for a pawn

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means these words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a1 is the corner square where the queen's rook starts in chess notation, written A1 with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A chess move description: king and pawn positioned beside a rook's corner, a decisive gambit in a key game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns ON + AI (A1) upwards to IANO. The surface is all chess, but 'key play' means playing on piano keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the dominant instrument in keyboard performance, the centrepiece of playing on keys.

clue.text: Turning to smother daughter in act of flattery

indicators.note: to smother means to cover entirely, so the turning word surrounds the daughter letter

parts.note: wheeling is turning in a circle
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent smothers a daughter with affection while turning about, all a show of flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxing someone with sweet talk to get what you want is a flattering act, so the gerund fits.

clue.text: River rising, unusually heavy rain primarily the cause

definitions.text: River rising, unusually heavy rain primarily the cause

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of each of the words river, unusually, heavy and rain

explanation.surface: A news report on a flood: the river rose and freak downpours were mainly to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the picture of a German river in flood, while the opening letters of four of its words spell the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is a German tributary of the Rhine, and the clue describes it swelling after a deluge.

clue.text: Captains shelled seafood

indicators.note: shelled means the outer casing is stripped, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: skippers are captains of ships or teams

explanation.surface: Ship captains tuck into seafood with the shells removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' strips the outer S and S from SKIPPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a split, smoked herring, a classic British breakfast fish.

clue.text: Maybe dumb down in Sydney if travelling

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to simplify their speech when touring Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SYDNEYIF. 'Maybe' marks dumbing down as one way of doing this.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a sanitised, simplified Hollywood-cartoon treatment is one way to dumb it down.

clue.text: Instrument found in box office after brief speculative view

indicators.note: after means the box office letters follow the shortened word
brief means the speculative view word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a theory is a speculative view

explanation.surface: A musical instrument turns up at the ticket desk after a quick hypothetical look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts THEORY to THEOR; 'found in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorbo is a large bass lute with an extended neck, a Baroque instrument.

clue.text: Monster conger-eel seen off and on

indicators.note: off and on means letters are taken and skipped in turn, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A huge eel is sighted now and then, like a sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' skips C, takes O, skips N, takes G and so on, giving O, G, R, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of fairy tales, a monster.

clue.text: Old celebrity couple replacing son in finale about missing female

indicators.note: about means the whole result is turned round to read backwards
replacing means the couple word takes the place of the son letter
missing means the female letter is left out of the finale word

parts.note: the finish is the finale or end
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a duo is a couple or pair

explanation.surface: A celebrity couple step in for a son at the end of a show, minus a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: FINISH without F ('missing female') is INISH; DUO 'replacing' S makes INIDUOH, and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was a famous early twentieth-century escapologist, a star of a bygone era.

clue.text: A tender kisser, Duncan regularly strays

indicators.note: strays suggests the letters wander from their places into a new order
regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of Duncan

explanation.surface: A gentle lover named Duncan has a habit of being unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives UCN from Duncan; 'strays' mixes it with KISSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends invalids is a carer, so 'a tender' here means one who tends the ill.

clue.text: Mature, wise men finally settled on epitaph

indicators.note: settled on means the final letters come after and rest upon the epitaph letters

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the classic gravestone epitaph

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the words wise and men

explanation.surface: Elders agree at last on the wording for a gravestone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E and N, which come after RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to mature, as fruit does when it becomes ready to eat.

clue.text: Clean seats returned around end of June

indicators.note: around means the reversed seats go round the letter from June
returned means the seats word is read backwards

parts.note: pews are seats in a church

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of June

explanation.surface: Church benches are put back after a cleaning at the close of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes SWEP from PEWS, and 'around' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep a floor is to clean it with a broom.

clue.text: Innocent type almost a victim, a sucker to some

indicators.note: almost means the innocent word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lamb is the archetype of innocence
prey is a victim of a predator

explanation.surface: A naive person is nearly a target, and some would call them a sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' looks like slang for a dupe, but the fish clamps on with a round sucking mouth; 'to some' admits the name is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that latches onto prey with a jawless sucking disc.

clue.text: Crazy displays behind lorry

indicators.note: in a down clue behind means the first part sits above the second

parts.note: to moon is to display one's bare bottom, so moons means displays
a truck is a lorry

explanation.surface: Someone mad shows off a bare bottom behind a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displays' is in the cheeky British sense of baring one's backside at people; 'behind' places it above the lorry in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstruck once meant driven mad by the moon, so it means crazy or dazed.

clue.text: Group kind of play about when adult's not there

indicators.note: about tells us the letters are turned about into a new order
not there says the adult letter is absent from the jumbled pool

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A type of drama goes on when no grown-ups are present.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A ('adult's not there') from KINDOFPLAY and 'about' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink Floyd were a celebrated British progressive rock band, a musical group.

clue.text: Friends, perhaps outside city, moan anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any order at all, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pals perhaps complain about life beyond the city limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges OUTSIDECITYMOAN. 'Friends' is the TV show, not companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends was a hugely popular American sitcom, an example of this TV genre, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Romantic writer ultimately writes terrifying tale

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of writes

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening story

explanation.surface: A Romantic author finally pens a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' means of the Romantic movement, not a writer of love stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Old drivers crashing into base tramp in Roman town

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: crashing into means the old drivers letters burst into the tramp word

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Elderly motorists smash into a down-and-out at the foot of a Roman settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motorists' breakdown club, and 'base' is the maths constant e, not a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eboracum was the Latin name of the Roman city that is now York.

clue.text: Cushion idiot owing debt?

indicators.note: owing means the idiot is 'in hock', placed inside the debt word

parts.note: to be in hock is to be in debt, so hock stands for debt
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool in debt has only a cushion to sit on.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone owing is 'in hock', so 'owing' puts ASS in HOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a padded cushion for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: Sewage initially affected gut of big fish

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of sewage

parts.note: camp means affected, theatrical and exaggerated

indicators.note: gut of means the innermost letter of big

explanation.surface: Sewage first hit the stomach of a large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big fish' looks like a phrase, but 'gut of' takes I from 'big' and 'fish' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, breaded and fried, a seafood dish loosely called fish.

clue.text: Black pen for penning love letters?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the pig pen surrounds the love letters

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
love is zero in tennis, written O, so two love letters are O and O

explanation.surface: Black ink for writing romantic letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love letters' looks like romance, but it is two Os (love = nil = O).
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in soot is sooty, so sooty means black or dark-coloured.

clue.text: Girl in survey at last checked — but not quite

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of survey
but not quite means the checked word stops one letter short

parts.note: vetted means checked or examined

explanation.surface: A girl is included in a survey that was, in the end, only partly verified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is just a link; 'at last' applies only to 'survey', and 'checked' is a past-tense synonym, then trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette is a French girl's name, so it defines a girl.

clue.text: Jacob's mate possibly on river vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting on top of the river letter

parts.note: Jacob's wife Rachel was named from the Hebrew for ewe, and Jacob's sheep are a breed, so his mate might be a ewe

explanation.surface: A biblical wife possibly boards a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacob's mate' is a ewe: Jacob sheep are a breed, and Rachel means ewe. 'vessel' is a jug, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug for water, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: One sought on line taps an ISP from the east

indicators.note: from the east in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: AOL is an internet service provider
taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

explanation.surface: Someone searched for online uses a connection from an Asian internet provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses AOL to LOA. 'on line' looks like the internet, but it is an angler's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The loach is a small freshwater fish that anglers might try to catch.

clue.text: African doctor also getting reported

indicators.note: getting reported means the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: Doctor Who is the TV time traveller, and also means too, giving 'who too'

explanation.surface: An African physician is also in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor gives 'Who', from the TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are one of the main ethnic groups of Rwanda and Burundi in Africa.

clue.text: Drop proceedings relating to non-capital sentences

parts.note: to lower something is to drop it
a case is a set of legal proceedings

explanation.surface: Abandoning a prosecution for sentences other than the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-capital sentences' looks legal, meaning no death penalty, but it means text with no capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters are those that are not capitals, so text in them is uncapitalised.

clue.text: Course adopted by English Lord portraying feeling of power? On the contrary

definitions.text: feeling of power? On the contrary

indicators.note: adopted by means the course is taken inside the lord word

parts.note: My Lord! is an exclamation, so lord gives MY
a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: An English peer finds a way of displaying a sense of his own authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'feeling of power' to 'power of feeling', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the ability to share and understand others' emotions, a power of feeling.

clue.text: Vehicle returned — still missing one item on forecourt?

indicators.note: returned means the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: missing means the one letter is absent from the still word

parts.note: still means quiet or calm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A car is sent back still lacking one part on a garage forecourt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forecourt' suggests a garage, but it is the front part of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player uses this stringed bat near the net, the forecourt of a tennis court.
